also: he always makes fun of me

evidence: Plaut. Trin. 2.4.45: bonīs tuīs rēbus meās rēs irrīdēs malās (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: make sport of, make a fool of
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.39.123: et vōs ab illō irrīdēminī et ipsī illum vicissim ēlūditis (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Quinct. 55: rīdet nostram āmentiam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Milder than dērīdeō, says Lewis & Short: laughing at someone rather than jeering.

evidence: Suet. Aug. 4: sīc taxat Augustum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 33: don’t tease him, nōlī eum taxāre
terms.comment: Traupman gives it for “tease”, but in Lewis & Short it is to reproach someone with a fault, a post-Augustan word (Suetonius, Pliny). For teasing use rīdēre or irrīdēre; taxāre is entered under criticism.

phrases.english: He always makes fun of me.
He always makes fun of me.
